title: Strong vs weak acids
examples: What does the strength of an acid really mean in chemistry?
How do I tell if an acid is strong or weak?
Does a high concentration mean a strong acid?

explain.say: Today we will look at strong and weak acids. We will compare how they behave in water.
A strong acid completely breaks apart in water. This means it ionises fully.

items: Acid Molecule → H+ ion + Anion ion

explain.say: A weak acid only partially breaks apart in water. It does not ionise completely.

items: Acid Molecule ⇌ H+ ion + Anion ion

explain.say: Concentration is the amount of acid dissolved in a given volume. It is measured in moles per litre.
The degree of ionisation tells us how much of the acid actually breaks apart. This is a percentage.
In real life, stomach acid is a weak acid. It only partially ionises in your body fluids.

faq.q: Does a high concentration always mean a strong acid?
faq.a: No, concentration and strength are two different ideas. A highly concentrated weak acid will still only ionise partially.
asks: If I make it more concentrated, does it become stronger?

faq.q: What is the difference between ionisation and dissociation?
faq.a: For acids, these terms are often used interchangeably. They both refer to the process of breaking apart in water to form ions.
asks: Do I use ionisation or dissociation?
Are these words the same in chemistry?

faq.q: How can I calculate the degree of ionisation?
faq.a: You usually need to set up an equilibrium expression involving the initial concentration and the amount that has reacted.
asks: What formula do I use for this?
Can you show me the calculation steps?

faq.q: Are strong acids always more dangerous than weak acids?
faq.a: While strong acids are highly reactive, the danger depends on concentration and the acid itself. Always treat all acids with care.
asks: Is strength the only measure of danger?

faq.q: What happens when I mix a strong acid with water?
faq.a: The strong acid will rapidly dissociate, releasing a large amount of hydrogen ions into the water.
asks: What is the reaction with water?
Is the reaction fast or slow?

facts: Strong acids, like hydrochloric acid, ionise completely in water.
Weak acids, like acetic acid, only ionise to an extent in water.
Concentration measures the amount of acid present in a solution.
The degree of ionisation measures the percentage of acid molecules that break apart.

quiz.say: Which statement correctly describes a strong acid in water?

options.show: Its concentration must be very low.
options.say: Its concentration must be very low.

options.show: It requires a catalyst to break apart.
options.say: It requires a catalyst to break apart.

quiz.why: Strong acids are defined by their ability to break apart fully in water.

wrong.0: This describes a weak acid, not a strong one.
wrong.1: Concentration is separate from acid strength.
wrong.2: Strong acids break apart naturally in water without needing a catalyst.

quiz.say: If a solution has a high concentration but is a weak acid, what is true?

options.show: It will have a higher potential amount of ions.
options.say: It will have a higher potential amount of ions.

options.show: It will behave like a strong acid.
options.say: It will behave like a strong acid.

options.show: It will have zero degree of ionisation.
options.say: It will have zero degree of ionisation.

quiz.why: More starting material means more ions can form, even if only a small percentage breaks apart.

wrong.0: Acids, by definition, release hydrogen ions making the solution acidic.
wrong.2: Strength is determined by the chemical bond, not just the amount.
wrong.3: It must ionise to some small degree to be considered an acid.

quiz.say: A solution of sulfuric acid (H2SO4) is very concentrated. Is it strong or weak?

options.show: It is classified as a strong acid.
options.say: It is classified as a strong acid.

options.show: It is weak because it is a polyprotic acid.
options.say: It is weak because it is a polyprotic acid.

options.show: It is weak because of its high concentration.
options.say: It is weak because of its high concentration.

options.show: It is neutral because it is a strong acid.
options.say: It is neutral because it is a strong acid.

quiz.why: Sulfuric acid is known chemically to ionise almost completely in water.

wrong.1: Its ability to ionise is still strong overall.
wrong.2: Concentration does not determine the inherent strength of the acid.
wrong.3: Strong acids always make solutions acidic, not neutral.
